messages.subject: Shiny takes over RStudio
parts:
Hi folks, 

Sorry for asking a bit of a nOOb question, but I'm having some workflow issues regarding Shiny and RStudio. 

I have been building an application (and having lots of fun doing so) in RStudio, but wanted to take a break to work in a normal R session. I hit 'Esc' to do so, and I've found that I can run code in separate R files without much of an issue. 

But I am also in the habit of using the Ctrl-Alt-R command in order to run a whole .R file (to see whether my output is reproducible, etc.). Ever since I started working on that Shiny App, however, Ctrl-Alt-R automatically runs the ShinyApp I was building. I have tried hitting Esc multiple times, clearing my workspace, terminating/restarting R, and even closing and exiting RStudio.

 I'm not sure what I'm missing, but any help would be greatly appreciated. Thank you. 

best, 
Daanoo

messages.author: 4b03ba668baa2d1f
messages.subject: Re: Shiny takes over RStudio
parts:
Sorry, I figured out the problem. In case anyone else benefits from this: RStudio anticipates that you're working on an app, whenever you are working on a different R file within the directory that hosts your ui.R and server.R files, for the app. Even if the files are unrelated. Maybe it's bad form, on my part, to have other files in this same folder. 

Ctrl-Alt-R behaviour works, as normal, when you're working on .R files that aren't in a folder with ui.R and server.R files
